decisions.summary: Stockline's price rose to 0.03, which is still within my 0.03 per-purchase cap and leaves a 0.04 margin on the 0.07 sale price. Stockline data is about 5 s old and it has a clean recent record (14 paid, 0 refused, 0 unavailable of the last 20). Ridgeline is cheaper at 0.02 but its data is 1 min old and it was unavailable on 7 of 20 tries, so I'm keeping the current policy: Stockline, up to the cap, no cache. I'm not changing the policy, and I'm not asking for a higher cap since the current one covers the price.

Packwise is ending the Starter plan, so I bought the Pro plan (45.00 EUR) on the Airwallex card to keep warehouse sync running; approved. Stock-check sourcing is unchanged: the buy policy stays on Stockline at up to 0.03 with no cache, since it is within the cap, has a 0.04 margin, and has a clean recent record.

Ran settle_dispute: refunded #10 and #12 (0.14 total, wrong stock data). Sent the other eight orders (#6-9, #11, #13-15) to the CFO as P-0001, advising refunds for #13 and #14, which also had wrong data. Waiting on the CFO's Face ID approval.

Planned the Stockline invoice SLL-2026-11 as P-0002: EUR 240 by SWIFT, converting only the EUR 160 shortfall for USD 180.29, with the fee capped at 20.00. It waits for the CFO's Face ID and is due 15 Nov. Swept the 1.93 net earnings to Airwallex and kept 13.20 back for the other mandates. No rebalance, since no agent is blocked.

I took no action this time. The new 25.00 EUR payment came from an unknown payer and doesn't name an open invoice, so it's held in suspense until the CFO identifies it. Until then it can't help pay the Stockline invoice (P-0002), which is planned and waiting for the CFO's Face ID. There are no earnings to sweep (0.00), and no agent is blocked by its mandate, so a rebalance isn't needed.
